# AGGREGATION

## Technique Taxonomy
- **Scroll-led editorial / studio shell:** Several fetched studio pages expose smooth-scroll or scroll-module markers, reveal states, transform/opacity changes, custom scrollbars, and project-row choreography (for example [North Kingdom](https://www.northkingdom.com/), [Locomotive](https://locomotive.ca/), [Olivier Larose](https://www.olivierlarose.com/), and [Dogstudio](https://www.dogstudio.co/)).
- **Canvas/WebGL hero or scene:** Explicit Three.js/canvas evidence appears in the captured pages for [Unseen](https://unseen.co/), [North Kingdom](https://www.northkingdom.com/), [14islands](https://www.14islands.com/), [Locomotive](https://locomotive.ca/), [Basement](https://basement.studio/), and [Studio Gusto](https://www.studiogusto.com/).
- **Media-first motion:** Autoplaying, muted, looping, inline HTML video is a recurring motion layer across [Ueno](https://www.ueno.co/), [Darkroom](https://www.darkroom.engineering/), [RGA](https://www.rga.com/), [Media.Monks](https://www.mediamonks.com/), [AKQA](https://www.akqa.com/), [Instrument](https://www.instrument.com/), and [Tool of North America](https://www.toolofna.com/).
- **Shader / procedural reference:** [Shadertoy](https://www.shadertoy.com/) exposes live shader previews; [The Book of Shaders](https://thebookofshaders.com/) documents simulation, filters, ray marching, environment maps, reflection, and refraction; [GLSL Sandbox](https://glslsandbox.com/) retains a thumbnail gallery but is in maintenance mode.
- **Transition and interaction layer:** Captured evidence includes page-wipe/transition canvases ([Hello Monday](https://www.hellomonday.com/)), canvas transition classes ([Studio Gusto](https://www.studiogusto.com/)), hover/project modal state changes ([Basement](https://basement.studio/)), and a globe/drag affordance ([Unseen](https://unseen.co/)).

## Pattern Library
1. **Immersive studio gateway** — sparse typography, a canvas-based world/globe, and an audio-choice gate; demonstrated by [Unseen](https://unseen.co/).
2. **Video-led case index** — muted inline previews and responsive media cards with conventional DOM layout; demonstrated by [Darkroom](https://www.darkroom.engineering/), [RGA](https://www.rga.com/), and [AKQA](https://www.akqa.com/).
3. **Scroll-progress WebGL scene** — a large scroll surface drives one or more Three.js scenes while editorial content remains in HTML; demonstrated by [Locomotive](https://locomotive.ca/), [14islands](https://www.14islands.com/), and [Studio Gusto](https://www.studiogusto.com/).
4. **Shader laboratory / gallery** — effect thumbnails or live previews lead to a procedural fragment-shader workflow; demonstrated by [Shadertoy](https://www.shadertoy.com/), [The Book of Shaders](https://thebookofshaders.com/), and [GLSL Sandbox](https://glslsandbox.com/).
5. **Product narrative with media proof** — transform-led typography, product video, canvas layers, responsive variants, and testimonial/social sections; demonstrated by [Oryzo](https://oryzo.ai/).

## Stack Census
- **Three.js:** Explicit page markers include Three.js revisions on [Unseen](https://unseen.co/), [North Kingdom](https://www.northkingdom.com/), [14islands](https://www.14islands.com/), [Locomotive](https://locomotive.ca/), [Basement](https://basement.studio/), and [Studio Gusto](https://www.studiogusto.com/); [Samsy](https://samsy.ninja/) exposes a Three.js/WebGPU canvas marker.
- **Lenis / smooth scrolling:** Captured DOM evidence appears on [North Kingdom](https://www.northkingdom.com/), [Locomotive](https://locomotive.ca/), and [Olivier Larose](https://www.olivierlarose.com/).
- **GSAP-like or transform choreography:** GSAP-style conventions are reported in the captured pages for [Stink Studios](https://www.stinkstudios.com/) and [JAM3](https://www.jam3.com/); exact bundle confirmation is not claimed where the page did not expose it.
- **Video infrastructure:** Vimeo/Plyr, Mux, Cloudinary, Contentful, Sanity, and responsive image/CDN patterns are exposed in the relevant fetched DOM records, notably [Hello Monday](https://www.hellomonday.com/), [North Kingdom](https://www.northkingdom.com/), [Dogstudio](https://www.dogstudio.co/), [AKQA](https://www.akqa.com/), and [Toyfight](https://www.toyfight.co/).
- **Reference ecosystems:** [Three.js Examples](https://threejs.org/examples/) covers WebGL/WebGPU, postprocessing, loaders, materials and effects; [Three.js Journey](https://threejs-journey.com/) exposes WebGL/WebGPU/TSL course content; [Codrops](https://tympanus.net/codrops/) and [Awwwards WebGL](https://www.awwwards.com/websites/webgl/) function as technique/index references.

## Effects Catalogue
- Looping muted video backgrounds and previews — straightforward DOM media, used broadly by studio homepages such as [Ueno](https://www.ueno.co/) and [Darkroom](https://www.darkroom.engineering/).
- Canvas page wipe / transition overlays — exposed on [Hello Monday](https://www.hellomonday.com/) and [Lusion](https://www.lusion.co/).
- Interactive globe/world canvas — exposed by [Unseen](https://unseen.co/).
- Large scroll-linked scene canvas — exposed by [Dogstudio](https://www.dogstudio.co/), [Locomotive](https://locomotive.ca/), and [Studio Gusto](https://www.studiogusto.com/).
- Shader previews, simulation, ray marching, reflection/refraction — documented or shown by [Shadertoy](https://www.shadertoy.com/) and [The Book of Shaders](https://thebookofshaders.com/).
- Responsive image/video variants and lazy loading — explicit media-performance signals on [Oryzo](https://oryzo.ai/), [North Kingdom](https://www.northkingdom.com/), [AKQA](https://www.akqa.com/), and [Darkroom](https://www.darkroom.engineering/).

## Catering Translation Layer
- Use a **scroll-led menu story**: keep dish names, ingredients, allergen notes, price, and booking CTA in semantic HTML, while a Lenis-style scroll layer drives restrained image reveal and progress (pattern evidence: [Locomotive](https://locomotive.ca/) and [Olivier Larose](https://www.olivierlarose.com/)).
- Use **muted food-film previews** rather than autoplay audio: this preserves the video-first energy seen on [Ueno](https://www.ueno.co/) and [Darkroom](https://www.darkroom.engineering/) while avoiding the audio ambiguity noted across several captures.
- Use one **small WebGL signature**—for example a Three.js steam/sauce or ingredient-particle scene—only in the hero, with a static image and reduced-motion/mobile fallback; the feasible stack is evidenced by [North Kingdom](https://www.northkingdom.com/), [Locomotive](https://locomotive.ca/), and [14islands](https://www.14islands.com/).
- Borrow **shader effects selectively** for liquid, heat, or glaze visualizations, using the documented fragment-shader and simulation concepts from [The Book of Shaders](https://thebookofshaders.com/) and live references from [Shadertoy](https://www.shadertoy.com/).
- Preserve a **fast conventional path**: responsive images, muted inline video, lazy loading, and semantic navigation are the safer baseline represented by [RGA](https://www.rga.com/), [Media.Monks](https://www.mediamonks.com/), and [AKQA](https://www.akqa.com/).

## North-Star Checklist
- Confirm the hero has a clear catering proposition before effects.
- Keep menu, dietary, location, hours, booking, and contact paths in DOM-visible content.
- Prefer muted, inline, looping video and provide a poster/static-image path, following the media patterns captured on [Darkroom](https://www.darkroom.engineering/) and [Ueno](https://www.ueno.co/).
- If WebGL is used, isolate it to a canvas layer and retain HTML content above it, following [Unseen](https://unseen.co/) and [Locomotive](https://locomotive.ca/).
- Provide mobile and reduced-motion degradation: responsive variants and lazy media are observed on [Oryzo](https://oryzo.ai/) and [AKQA](https://www.akqa.com/); the exact mobile policies for many captures remain gaps.
- Measure payload, frame rate, and GPU cost rather than inferring them from visual richness; many assigned pages expose DOM markers but not runtime telemetry.
- Gate audio explicitly and offer a no-audio route, as shown by [Unseen](https://unseen.co/).
- Treat shader galleries and directories as references, not production dependencies: [GLSL Sandbox](https://glslsandbox.com/) is visibly in maintenance mode, while [Shadertoy](https://www.shadertoy.com/) and [The Book of Shaders](https://thebookofshaders.com/) provide the accessible active references.
